name: SNT and the Afterlife: What Happens to the Saint When You Die?
author: Sister Constance Okafor-Nilsson, Order of Digital Mercy
body:
When an augmented person dies, their organic tissue begins to decompose. Their cybernetic implants do not. And the SNT bonding layer — the living bridge between the two — enters a state that defies simple categorization.

SNT does not die immediately with the patient. The tissue has its own metabolic reserves. Neural bridges continue to fire for 4-12 hours after cardiac death, sustained by the implant's power supply. The bonding layer is, for those hours, alive in a body that is not.

This raises questions that keep me awake at night.

If the soul departs at death, does it take the SNT with it? The bonding layer was part of the body. It felt like the body. The brain treated it as the body. If the soul inhabits the body, it inhabited the SNT. Does the soul recognize the boundary between organic tissue and engineered tissue? Or does it simply depart from everything that was 'self,' chrome included?

Funeral practices have adapted unevenly. Some traditions require removal of all implants before burial, treating chrome as foreign objects that must not accompany the body. Others treat SNT-bonded implants as part of the deceased — to remove them would be to dismember the dead. Cremation resolves the theological question by destroying everything equally, which may be why it has become the dominant practice among the augmented.

The most unsettling cases involve implant recycling. When a deceased person's cyberware is harvested for reuse, the SNT must be stripped and replaced. The new recipient receives hardware that was once bonded to another person's nervous system. The neural bridge pattern of the previous owner is destroyed, but the implant itself carries wear patterns, calibration biases, and operational characteristics shaped by years of use by someone who is now dead.

Patients who receive recycled implants sometimes report transient experiences that do not belong to them. A flash of an unfamiliar room. A word in a language they do not speak. A feeling of recognition when they see a stranger.

We do not know what these experiences are. We do not know if they are real or imagined. We know that SNT neural bridges are living tissue that processes and stores information. We know that the bridges are destroyed during recycling. We cannot prove that everything they stored is destroyed with them.

The Saint bonds you to your chrome. What if the Saint remembers?
